blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Southbank? 2026 Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of extending your Southbank apartment or townhouse? We break down costs per square metre, council fees, and timelines for 2026.
body: Home extensions in Southbank vary hugely depending on whether you're adding a second storey, a rear extension, or bumping out into a balcony. As a rough guide, expect to pay between $3,500 and $6,000 per square metre for a quality build. That includes demolition, structural work, finishes, and permits. Kmercial always provides a fixed-price quote after inspecting your property, so you know exactly where you stand before work begins.

One of the biggest cost drivers in Southbank is council compliance. The City of Melbourne and Port Phillip councils have strict heritage overlays and height restrictions. If your property is in a heritage precinct, you may need extra consultant reports — sometimes adding $5,000–$10,000 to your budget. We handle all council liaison and permit applications, so you don't have to navigate the red tape yourself.

Another factor is site access. Many Southbank homes are apartments or townhouses with limited street access. If we can't get a skip bin or materials directly to your door, costs go up. We often use logistics plans and small vehicles to minimise disruption. We'll always advise you on access challenges during the free consultation — no surprises.

Timing is also crucial. In Melbourne, the best building months are October to April when the weather is dry. Pouring concrete in winter requires extra care and curing time. We schedule major concrete and roofing work in the warmer months to avoid delays. A typical extension takes 12–20 weeks depending on complexity.

Don't forget internal finishes. Your choice of tiles, benchtops, tapware, and lighting can swing the total cost by 30% or more. We help you choose products that suit your budget and style, and we buy trade-priced materials to save you money. Many Southbank clients go for minimalist, high-end finishes that add value.

Finally, always budget a 10% contingency. Even with the best planning, unexpected issues like termite damage or old wiring can crop up. Kmercial includes a contingency allowance in our fixed quotes and will only use it if absolutely necessary. That way you're never left with a half-finished extension.

blogPosts.title: Renovating an Apartment in Southbank? Read This First
blogPosts.excerpt: Apartment renovations in Southbank come with extra rules, from owners corporation approvals to structural changes. Our guide covers everything.
body: Renovating an apartment in Southbank is different to renovating a house. You need approval from the owners corporation (OC) as well as council permission. The OC might restrict working hours, waste disposal, and even the colour of your front door. We always check the OC rules before starting a quote, so you know what's allowed.

Structural changes — like knocking down a wall or moving a kitchen — often require a building permit and engineering sign-off. In many Southbank high-rises, the structure is concrete slab and column, so walls may be non-loadbearing. But you can't assume. We arrange a site inspection with an engineer to verify what's possible.

Plumbing and electrical work in apartments is also complex. Rerouting pipes in a concrete slab is expensive. You may need to chase walls or build bulkheads. We've done hundreds of apartment renos in Southbank, so we know the tricks to keep costs down while meeting compliance.

Soundproofing is another big concern in apartment blocks. You need to meet the Building Code minimum for inter-tenancy noise insulation. We use acoustic batts, resilient channels, and double-glazed windows where required. This adds cost but protects you from neighbour complaints.

Budget for at least 15% extra on apartment renos because of the unknowns. Once we open up the walls, we might find old asbestos, outdated wiring, or corroded pipes. Kmercial gives you a clear report before we proceed, so you can decide whether to go ahead or adjust the scope.

Finally, work with a builder who knows the OC process. We submit all documentation on your behalf, attend OC meetings if needed, and ensure work complies with building insurance requirements. That's why so many Southbank apartment owners trust Kmercial for their renovation.

blogPosts.title: Fixed-Price vs Cost-Plus Building Contracts: Which is Better for Your Southbank Build?
blogPosts.excerpt: Confused about building contracts? We explain the pros and cons of fixed-price vs cost-plus, and why Southbank homeowners prefer fixed-price.
body: When you build or renovate, the contract type you choose affects your budget, stress level, and final result. In Victoria, the two most common are fixed-price and cost-plus. Fixed-price means you agree on a total cost upfront; cost-plus means you pay the actual cost of materials and labour plus a management fee. At Kmercial we only use fixed-price contracts for residential work.

Cost-plus sounds flexible but often leads to budget blowouts. You don't know the final number until the project is finished. If material prices rise or the builder takes longer, you pay more. In 2023-2026 we've seen timber and steel costs fluctuate by up to 30%. Under cost-plus, that's your problem. Under fixed-price, it's ours.

Fixed-price contracts require a detailed scope of works. We spend time getting the design right and specifying every material, finish, and fitting. This means fewer variations. If you change your mind after signing, we quote the variation separately. Most Southbank clients prefer this because it gives them peace of mind.

Some owners worry that fixed-price means the builder will cut corners to save money. That's why you choose the right builder. Kmercial has a reputation for quality — we don't cut corners because our brand depends on doing the job right. Our fixed quotes include the exact products agreed, and we only substitute with prior approval.

What about large commercial builds? For those, cost-plus can be fair because the scope often changes. But for homes and apartments in Southbank, fixed-price is the standard. Make sure your contract is compliant with the Domestic Building Contracts Act 1995 (Vic). All our contracts include cooling-off periods and statutory warranties.

Before signing any contract, demand a clear list of inclusions and exclusions. We provide a full schedule with every item from tapware to tiles, so you know what's covered. No hidden extras. If you're considering a build in Southbank, we're happy to walk you through our contract and explain every clause.
